meta.title: At the Market · Al mercato
meta.source_url: Sample: hand-written VTT (lessons/raw/al_mercato_it.vtt), not a real video

sentences.en: Good morning, madam, what would you like today?

sentences.it: Buongiorno! Vorrei un chilo di pomodori, per favore.
sentences.en: Good morning! I'd like a kilo of tomatoes, please.
How much are they per kilo?

sentences.it: Va bene, e mi dia anche mezzo chilo di zucchine.
sentences.en: All right, and give me half a kilo of courgettes as well.

sentences.it: Perfetto. Ha anche del basilico fresco?
sentences.en: Perfect. Do you also have some fresh basil?

sentences.it: No, grazie, basta così. Quant'è in tutto?
sentences.en: No, thank you, that's all. How much is it altogether?

mcqs.q: How many tomatoes does the customer want to buy?
Besides tomatoes and courgettes, what does she ask for?
In the end, does she want anything else?

grammar.title: Vorrei… — the polite "I'd like"
grammar.use: Making a request in a shop, a restaurant or at the market. Far more polite than voglio (I want).
grammar.structure: Vorrei + noun / Vorrei + infinitive (Vorrei un chilo di pomodori / Vorrei comprare…)
grammar.example: Vorrei un chilo di pomodori, per favore.
grammar.explain: vorrei is the conditional of volere, first person singular: literally "I would want". Add per favore at the end to sound natural. Quantities always take di: un chilo DI pomodori, mezzo chilo DI zucchine, un litro DI latte.

grammar.title: Quanto costa / costano? — asking the price
grammar.use: costa for one item, costano for several.
grammar.structure: Quanto costa + singular noun? / Quanto costano + plural noun? / Quant'è (in tutto)?
grammar.example: Quanto costano al chilo? — Quant'è in tutto?
grammar.explain: Here costano refers back to the pomodori (plural). al chilo = a + il chilo, "per kilo". When you pay, ask for the total with Quant'è in tutto? (Quant'è is the elided form of Quanto è).

grammar.title: del / della / dei… — the partitive "some"
grammar.use: An unspecified amount of something, especially with uncountable nouns.
grammar.structure: di + definite article: del (il) / dello (lo) / della (la) / dell' / dei (i) / degli (gli) / delle (le)
grammar.explain: del basilico = some basil. The quiz options del pane and delle patate use the same pattern. After a Sì, people usually go straight to the quantity: un mazzetto (a small bunch), un chilo, and so on.

grammar.title: Mi dia… — the polite imperative (Lei form)
grammar.use: Requests to a shopkeeper, a waiter, anyone you address with Lei.
grammar.structure: Mi dia + noun (dia is the Lei imperative of dare) · also: Mi dica (tell me), Mi scusi (excuse me)
grammar.example: Va bene, e mi dia anche mezzo chilo di zucchine.
grammar.explain: The whole dialogue uses Lei, the formal "you": cosa desidera, ha anche…, mi dia, ecco a lei. With a friend you'd say dammi (tu form). Note the word order: anche sits between the verb and the noun: mi dia ANCHE mezzo chilo.

vocab.mean: to want, to wish (shopkeepers' Cosa desidera? = What would you like?)
a kilo / half a kilo (chilo is short for chilogrammo)
that's all, that's enough (the set phrase to end a purchase)
